title: The Patents Act, 1970
summary: Primary Indian patent statute governing patentability, novelty, inventive step, examination procedures, and opposition mechanisms.

title: The Patents Act, 1970 — Section 3(p)
summary: Statutory bar prohibiting patents on traditional knowledge or an aggregation/duplication of known properties of traditionally known components unless non-obvious synergistic efficacy is empirically proven.

title: The Patents Act, 1970 — Section 3(d) & 3(e)
summary: Section 3(d) mandates proof of significantly enhanced therapeutic efficacy for new forms/derivatives of known substances; Section 3(e) bars mere admixtures lacking synergistic interaction.

title: Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL)
summary: Authoritative database of codified traditional medicine (Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani, Yoga) cited by international patent examiners as prior art to reject erroneous natural product claims.

title: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 & Amendment 2023
summary: Establishes India's ABS framework. Section 6(1) mandates NBA approval prior to patent grant for inventions using Indian bio-resources; Section 3 governs foreign access (Form I); Section 7 governs SBB intimation with exemptions for cultivated plants under BMC Certificate of Origin.

title: The Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 & Rules, 1945
authority: Ministry of AYUSH & State Licensing Authorities
summary: Governs statutory licensing, Schedule T Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), heavy metal limits, and quality standards for Ayurvedic, Siddha, and Unani (ASU) medicines in India.

title: Drugs & Cosmetics Rules, 1945 — Rule 158B
summary: Statutory classification of ASU drugs: Rule 158B(I)(A) allows Form 25D licensing for Classical Formulations based on First Schedule textual evidence without clinical trials; Rule 158B(I)(B) governs Patent or Proprietary ASU medicines requiring safety/toxicity dossiers.

title: CDSCO Phytopharmaceutical Drug Regulations — Rule 2(eb)
legal_instrument: G.S.R. 918(E) & New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules
summary: Regulates purified and standardized botanical fractions containing minimum 4 bioactive markers, requiring IND submission and Phase I/II/III clinical trials under CDSCO SEC approval.

title: FSSAI (Ayurveda Aahar) Regulations, 2022
authority: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)
summary: Defines safety, labeling, and recipe standards for food prepared in accordance with authoritative Ayurvedic culinary texts. Strictly bars curative disease claims and Schedule E-1 poisonous herbs.

title: The Trade Marks Act, 1999
summary: Governs trademark registration in Class 5 (Pharmaceuticals/ASU) and Class 3 (Cosmetics). Section 9 bars generic Sanskrit/Ayurvedic terms; Section 11 prevents confusing similarity.

title: The Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999
summary: Protects region-specific medicinal goods and agricultural botanicals linked to geographical origin, requiring Authorized User certification.

title: The Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954
summary: Strictly prohibits misleading advertisements claiming cure or prevention for 54 specific chronic conditions (e.g. cancer, diabetes, arthritis, anxiety, sexual disorders).

title: US FDA 21 CFR Part 312 & Botanical Drug Development Guidance
authority: United States Food and Drug Administration (US FDA / CDER)
legal_instrument: Code of Federal Regulations Title 21, Part 312
summary: Governs IND applications and clinical trial authorizations for botanical drugs in the US. Outlines CMC batch-to-batch consistency, raw material authentication, Phase I/II safety/efficacy, and NDA approval pathway.

title: US FDA 21 CFR Part 111 — Dietary Supplement cGMP & DSHEA
authority: United States Food and Drug Administration (US FDA / CFSAN)
summary: Mandates current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) for manufacturing, packaging, labeling, or holding dietary supplements. Allows structure/function claims with mandatory FDA disclaimer; strictly bars disease cure claims.

title: 35 U.S. Code § 101 / § 102 / § 103 — Patent Subject Matter Eligibility
authority: United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO)
summary: Governs patentability under US law. Under Mayo/Alice precedents, natural extracts and products of nature are ineligible under § 101 unless transformed into markedly different compositions or synergistic combinations.

title: EU Directive 2004/24/EC — Traditional Herbal Medicinal Products Directive (THMPD)
summary: Provides a simplified registration procedure for traditional herbal medicinal products in the EU. Requires proof of 30 years continuous traditional medicinal use, including at least 15 years within the European Union.

title: EMA / HMPC Community Herbal Monographs & List Entries
authority: Committee on Herbal Medicinal Products (HMPC / EMA)
summary: Authoritative European Union scientific opinions on herbal substances covering 'well-established use' (demonstrated 10-year EU clinical efficacy) and 'traditional use' registrations.

title: Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT)
summary: Unified international procedure allowing patent applicants to preserve filing priority across 158 member countries via a single international application with an International Search Report (ISR).

title: Madrid System for the International Registration of Marks
summary: Single international application and management system for securing and maintaining trademark rights in Class 5/3 across up to 130 designated contracting parties.

title: Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit-Sharing
summary: International treaty establishing compliance measures to ensure prior informed consent (PIC) and mutually agreed terms (MAT) for cross-border utilization of genetic resources and traditional knowledge.

title: WIPO Treaty on IP, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge
summary: Historic WIPO treaty establishing a mandatory disclosure requirement in patent applications where claimed inventions are based on genetic resources or associated traditional knowledge.

title: EU Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 — Article 4 (Responsible Person)
legal_instrument: Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council
summary: Article 4 mandates that only cosmetic products for which a legal or natural person is designated within the Community as 'Responsible Person' shall be placed on the market. The Responsible Person shall ensure compliance with each cosmetic product's safety, GMP, PIF, CPNP notification, and SUE obligations.

title: EU Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 — Article 10 (Safety Assessment & CPSR)
authority: European Commission / Scientific Committee on Consumer Safety (SCCS)
legal_instrument: Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council
summary: Article 10 mandates that prior to placing a cosmetic product on the market, the Responsible Person shall ensure that the product has undergone a safety assessment on the basis of relevant information and that a Cosmetic Product Safety Report (CPSR) is drawn up in accordance with Annex I by a qualified safety assessor holding a recognized diploma in pharmacy, toxicology, medicine or similar discipline.

title: EU Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 — Article 11 (Product Information File - PIF)
authority: European Commission / Member State Competent Authorities
legal_instrument: Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council
summary: Article 11 requires the Responsible Person to keep a Product Information File (PIF) readily accessible in electronic or other format at the address specified on the label for a period of 10 years following the date on which the last batch was placed on the market. The PIF must contain the description of the cosmetic product, CPSR, manufacturing method conforming to ISO 22716 GMP, proof of claimed effects, and data on any animal testing.

title: EU Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 — Article 13 (CPNP Notification)
legal_instrument: Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council
summary: Article 13 dictates that prior to placing a cosmetic product on the market, the Responsible Person shall submit electronically to the European Commission via CPNP: product category and name, RP name and address, country of origin, Member State of first placing on market, presence of nanomaterials, and frame formulation for prompt medical treatment.

title: EU Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 — Article 16 (Nanomaterials)
legal_instrument: Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council
summary: Article 16 establishes that cosmetic products containing nanomaterials must be notified to the Commission electronically by the Responsible Person 6 months prior to placing on the market (except for colorants, preservatives, and UV filters listed in Annexes IV to VI). Notification must include identification, specifications, toxicological profile, and exposure conditions.

title: EU Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 — Article 23 (Communication of Serious Undesirable Effects - SUE)
authority: Member State Competent Authorities / European Commission
legal_instrument: Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council
summary: Article 23 governs cosmetovigilance, requiring that in the event of Serious Undesirable Effects (SUE), the Responsible Person and distributors shall without delay notify the competent authority of the Member State where the SUE occurred, detailing the type of SUE, product name, and corrective measures taken.

title: EU Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 — Annex I (Cosmetic Product Safety Report - CPSR)
subdomain: CPSR Part A & Part B Structure
summary: Annex I establishes the mandatory structure of the Cosmetic Product Safety Report (CPSR): Part A (Cosmetic Product Safety Information: quantitative formula, physical/chemical characteristics, stability, microbiological quality, impurities, packaging, normal and foreseeable use, exposure to the product/substances, toxicological profile) and Part B (Cosmetic Product Safety Assessment: assessment conclusion, labeled warnings and instructions of use, scientific reasoning, and safety assessor's credentials).
